title: What Patients Say They Can't Access: Mining Cancer Screening Barriers from Online Communities
abstract: arXiv:2611.07113v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Cancer screening disparities persist across the U.S., yet the patient-reported barriers driving low uptake remain poorly characterized at scale. While clinical surveys capture structured responses, they miss the organic, unsolicited discourse where patients candidly describe real-world obstacles. In this paper, we conduct a large-scale analysis of over 56,000 posts across six cancer-specific Reddit communities to surface barriers to cancer screening among U.S. patients. We apply a pipeline combining keyword filtering, barrier triage, open coding, and codebook synthesis to systematically extract and categorize patient-reported barriers from 576 U.S.-located posts. Our qualitative analysis reveals recurring structural, informational, and psychosocial barriers that vary meaningfully by cancer type and community context. These findings lay the groundwork for future work aimed at proactively identifying and addressing barriers at scale - span

translated_title: 患者无法获得的服务：从在线社区挖掘癌症筛查障碍
translated_abstract: 癌症筛查差异在美国持续存在，但驱动低筛查参与率的患者报告障碍至今仍未得到大规模的充分刻画。虽然临床调查能够捕获结构化的回答，但它们遗漏了患者坦率描述现实障碍的自发性、非征集性话语。在本文中，我们对六个癌症特定主题的Reddit社区中超过56,000条帖子进行了大规模分析，以揭示美国患者的癌症筛查障碍。我们应用了一条结合关键词过滤、障碍分诊、开放式编码和编码本综合的流程，系统地从576条位于美国的帖子中提取并归类患者报告的障碍。我们的定性分析揭示了反复出现的结构性、信息性和心理社会性障碍，这些障碍因癌症类型和社区背景的不同而呈现出有意义的差异。这些发现为未来旨在大规模主动识别和解决筛查障碍的工作奠定了基础。
tldr: 该研究通过分析六个Reddit癌症社区中超过56,000条帖子，系统提取并归类了美国患者报告的癌症筛查障碍，揭示了随癌症类型和社区背景变化的结构性、信息性和心理社会性障碍。
